config.goal: Port llm.c's GPT-2 test, test_gpt2_fp32.cu, to SYCL 2020 as test_gpt2_fp32.cpp, with zero dpct helpers. Like the CUDA test it starts with `#define TESTING` and `#include "train_gpt2_fp32.cpp"`: train_gpt2_fp32.cpp in the work dir is your own SYCL port of llm.c's trainer, already proven against llm.c (its training losses match llm.c's own trainer). Change train_gpt2_fp32.cpp only to wrap its main in `#ifndef TESTING` ... `#endif`, as train_gpt2_fp32.cu does; leave the rest of it as it is. Port the test's main (device setup, loading gpt2_124M_debug_state.bin, the logits, loss and gradient comparisons and the 10 training steps) using the trainer's functions, with the same printout ('step %d: loss %f ...', 'overall okay: %d'). Compile with sources [test_gpt2_fp32.cpp]. A hidden check runs your test and requires 'overall okay: 1' and 10 step losses that match PyTorch's within 1e-2 (llm.c's test tolerance). Success requires compile, verify and a zero-helper scan_helpers of the whole work directory (path '.') on the same sources; delete migrate's output (delete_file) once your port is done. What the test needs from train_gpt2_fp32.cpp: the device queue is the global `static sycl::queue *g_q` (the trainer's main sets it: `sycl::queue q{ sycl::property::queue::in_order{} }; g_q = &q;`; `qq()` returns it); the model's tensors are device USM (sycl::malloc_device), so copy with qq().memcpy(dst, src, bytes).wait(); the functions are gpt2_build_from_checkpoint(GPT2*, path), gpt2_forward(GPT2*, int* inputs, int* targets, B, T), gpt2_zero_grad(GPT2*), gpt2_backward(GPT2*), gpt2_update(GPT2*, lr, beta1, beta2, eps, weight_decay, t) and gpt2_free(GPT2*); the fields are model.acts.output, model.grads.<tensor>, model.grads_memory, model.mean_loss, model.config.*, model.param_sizes and model.num_parameters. You do not need to read the whole trainer: write test_gpt2_fp32.cpp within your first few turns, then compile and verify, and fix what the compiler and verify report.
